sources.note: "Weight 313 lbs (142 kg)"

dryWeight.method: No Nissan or measured VQ35HR weight was found (2007 service manual, Nissan USA press kits 2007-2009, Nissan's VQ35HR tech sheet, English and Japanese searches). Started from the only VQ35DE figure, 313 lb (142 kg; one forum weighing, dress level unknown), and added roughly 5-10 kg for the HR's ladder frame, 8.4 mm taller block, longer rods and larger crank journals, which Nissan lists but does not weigh. Rounded to 150 kg; treat it as about +/-20 kg. enginetechspecs.com prints 175 kg "complete with flywheel, without accessories" and 190 kg "with alternator, starter and manifolds", but that page contradicts the service manual elsewhere (hydraulic VTC on both cams, head-bolt torques), so it was not used.

crank.method: Neither the 2007 service manual (disassembly and SDS) nor Nissan's press material states crank, rod or piston materials for the VQ35HR. The VQ35DE crank is described as forged by 8020 Automotive and engine-specs.net (non-Nissan); the HR crank keeps the stroke with larger main and pin journals, and Nissan's 2009 kit calls it "micro-finished". Assumed forged, as the DE.

rods.method: Neither the 2007 service manual (disassembly and SDS) nor Nissan's press material states crank, rod or piston materials for the VQ35HR. The VQ35DE rods are described as forged steel by non-Nissan sources; the HR rods are 7.6 mm longer (Nissan) with 9 mm bolts instead of 8 mm (engine-specs.net). Assumed forged, as the DE.

pistons.method: Neither the 2007 service manual (disassembly and SDS) nor Nissan's press material states crank, rod or piston materials for the VQ35HR. Nissan mentions only asymmetric skirts (HR) and molybdenum coating (DE). Cast aluminium is assumed because nothing says forged; this is the least certain of the three.

value.note: The page does not say crank or wheel power; stored as crank power.

reportedLimits.context: Aggregator claim (mywikimotors.com) with no boost, fuel, rpm or duration given. Forum threads that discuss HR stock-internal limits (my350z.com, 350z-tech.com, nicoclub) were blocked, so nothing from them is used. Treat it as a rough community figure, not a tested limit. Known track weak point: oil pick-up starvation under sustained cornering (see notes).

sources.note: EM-100 and SDS EM-141, valve spring: "Installation height : 37.0 mm (1.457 in)" ... "Height during valve open : 26.8 mm (1.055 in)".

intakeLift.method: Nissan does not publish valve lift. The service manual's valve-spring data (2007 manual EM-100 and EM-141) give the installed height (37.00 mm) and the spring height with the valve fully open (26.8 mm); the difference, 10.2 mm, is the full valve lift the spring is specified for. The same springs are used on intake and exhaust. The lobes (cam height 45.865-46.055 mm intake) are 1 mm taller than the standard VQ35DE's, like the rev-up DE. mywikimotors.com (aggregator) prints 10.54 mm.

sources.title: Nissan Motor Co.: 2007 Nissan 350Z Service Manual, section EM "Engine Mechanical" (VQ35HR), revision November 2006 (PDF copy on Google Drive, linked from carmanualsclub.com)
sources.note: EM-100 and SDS EM-141, valve spring: "Installation height : 37.0 mm (1.457 in)" ... "Height during valve open : 26.8 mm (1.055 in)".

intakeLift.method: Nissan does not publish valve lift. The service manual's valve-spring data (2007 manual EM-100 and EM-141) give the installed height (37.00 mm) and the spring height with the valve fully open (26.8 mm); the difference, 10.2 mm, is the full valve lift the spring is specified for. The same springs are used on intake and exhaust. The lobes (cam height 45.865-46.055 mm intake) are 1 mm taller than the standard VQ35DE's, like the rev-up DE. mywikimotors.com (aggregator) prints 10.54 mm.
